title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

reading.body:
This is a false positive from an automated identification system, and it failed at the point where a machine alert becomes police action. A license-plate reader produced a match, and that match was treated as grounds for a stop at gunpoint rather than as a lead requiring verification. The system's output was wrong, and nothing between the alert and the armed response corrected it.

Catching it would have taken independent confirmation of the alert before officers acted, which is what the vendor itself says its alerts require. The agency's account locates the cause in the input conditions, an illegal tinted plate cover that it says caused the malfunction, which describes a system being relied on outside the conditions its accuracy depends on. That account comes from the sheriff's office, which also reviewed its own deputy's conduct and found it reasonable.

It is not established that the plate cover caused the misread, and the finding that the deputy acted reasonably is the agency's own conclusion rather than an independent adjudication.

reports.title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

summary: Steven Melvin, a 42-year-old motorist in York County, South Carolina, was reportedly held at gunpoint for more than five minutes after a Flock Safety license-plate reader misread the first letter of his plate and matched his BMW to a similar stolen vehicle. The sheriff’s office later said an illegal tinted plate cover caused the malfunction and found the deputy’s actions reasonable. Flock advised that alerts need independent confirmation before police action.
